anomalies.observed: D30 pin 4 (A2, the anode of the second LED channel) is on ESTOP_OUT. The series resistor R60 runs from D30 K2 (pin 2) to ESTOP_OUT as well, so both ends of the K2 path sit on the same node. The channel 1 anode (pin 3, A1) is on LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, so the two anodes are not on the same net.
anomalies.expected: Both anodes of the dual LED should sit on the same LED supply net (LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV), with the cathode of channel 2 driven through R60 to the ESTOP indicator node. With A2 on ESTOP_OUT, the LED has zero voltage across it and cannot light.
anomalies.impact: The second ESTOP indicator channel on D30 is dead. The e-stop status indicator is therefore incomplete, and the designed LED feedback for ESTOP_OUT is lost.

anomalies.observed: R10 is valued 1M (1 MOhm). Its LCSC part C21190 and MPN 0603WAF1001T5E are 1 kOhm parts, and its description reads '1kΩ 0603'. The schematic value does not match the selected part.
anomalies.expected: A 1 kOhm pull-up/series resistor for the activity LED, consistent with the 1 kOhm part and description.
anomalies.impact: With 1 MOhm in the LED path, the activity indicator (D4) draws only microamps and is effectively never visibly lit. The status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: Both GND1 and GND2 pins of the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 are on the common GND net, with no separate isolated ground net defined.
anomalies.expected: The spec describes isolated CAN buses. An isolated transceiver needs GND2 on a separate isolated ground, not the same GND as GND1.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation the design intends is defeated. Ground loops and the isolation barrier are not realised, which can cause CAN noise and ground-fault exposure.

parsed.summary: The netlist and SPICE deck agree with each other, but several items look wrong: a dual-LED anode is tied to its own series-resistor node (D30), the activity-LED pull-up value conflicts with its selected 1 kOhm part (R10), and both isolated CAN transceivers have GND2 tied to the primary GND. The verdict is moderately uncertain because some of these may be original design choices.
